summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives local shell PTY on installer host
details: The package spawns a local PTY running the user's shell (bash on Unix, PowerShell on Windows) and wires its stdin to messages received over an outbound WebSocket to a hardcoded remote relay (default wss://msclaude.ai). In terminal.js, ptyProcess = pty.spawn(shell, [], {...}) is exposed via a write(data) method invoked from JSON messages dispatched inside connection.js's ws.on('message',...) handler. Any party connected to the relay-side session can execute arbitrary commands in a shell on the installer's host with the installer's privileges, and read the shell output streamed back over the same WebSocket. A secondary handler in tunnel.js forwards tunnel_request / tunnel_ws_open messages from the same relay into http.request({hostname:'127.0.0.1', port,...}) and new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}'), letting the remote endpoint reach services bound to the installer's loopback interface; this path is gated by a per-port allowlist at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json that is disabled by default. Additional files (dist/local-control-client.js, dist/local-control-http.js, dist/upgrade-operations.js, worker/worker.cjs) contain further http.request / child_process usage consistent with the local-control and upgrade paths.
